summary: InferOps project boards, coding dispatch, the InferMind Wiki (its structure, page bodies and sections, and approval of drafted page proposals for publication) read-only custom tables, and one account connection per organization that opens the person's own boards and Wikis by reference, reached only through scoped bindings whose every read is an observation and every write an approved action. InferOps stays authoritative: nothing here stores a copy of its entities.

resources.scope: One project, by key, in one workspace the signed-in person holds. The workspace slug is resolved against their memberships when the Workshop mints the binding and fixed in its props; no session method takes a project, host, workspace or account. An issue of another project is refused exactly as an unknown one (NOT_FOUND).

reads.notes: The bound project's board, pending actions overlaid.
Fixed published service queries scoped to this project; joined-data observations exclude board-only collaborators.
Narrows to one issue of the bound project; its read() is an observation.

writes.notes: Body and expected head are fingerprinted; sent only when the queued action is applied.
Reverted only while the issue is still in the state it moved to.
Title and priority revert while the issue is still at the revision the update produced; a description change never reverts.

resources.scope: One project's software issues, bound by the same rules as a board, and only repositories on the wrapper's CODING_WORKBENCH_REPOS allowlist, checked at proposal and again at apply. A separate grant: a board binding never dispatches. InferOps additionally requires the person's issue:delegate.

writes.notes: A CONFLICT for a run that has already stopped counts as applied.

resources.scope: One InferMind workspace's Wiki the person holds; one of their InferOps workspaces is refused as having no Wiki. inferops://…/knowledge/document/<slug> references inside pages are returned, never resolved or bound.

reads.notes: The company root, the pillars with their Masters and filed pages, and the unfiled pages; only pages listDocuments shows.
The page's body (document-level), its lens-gated sections and its references, with pending edits overlaid.
InferOps' page-text contract: the body, else the visible sections, then a Master's generated structure block. A page with a body never merges its sections.

InferOps' drafted page proposals (proposal.list), newest first, at most 200, without principals; one waiting for an approval here is marked pending approve. NOT_FOUND while knowledge.wikiPublish.enabled is off in InferOps.
One proposal with its freshness for this reader (proposal.get): the target's and each cited section's current version, null where not visible.

writes.notes: InferOps' page PATCH is a strict compare-and-swap on the page version: apply sends the proposed version and is refused STALE_REVISION by any change since, even one that left the same body; InferOps replays only a retry of the same write under the same key. Reverted by a fresh write expecting the version the edit produced, under its own key.

InferOps' section PATCH takes no expected version and does not replay a key, so apply re-reads the section: at the proposed version it writes; already showing this body it counts as applied; otherwise it refuses as STALE_REVISION. Reverted while the section still shows the applied body at the applied version.

Approves one in_review proposal for publication (proposal.approve, knowledge:publish: Owner or Admin), which queues InferOps' publish job; nothing here publishes, and the applied action says approved, never published. The expected version is the proposal hash and cited sources read at staging (STALE_REVISION for any other). The replay is InferOps' own, by the same principal and hash on a decided proposal, not by the key, which is sent by convention only. Owner-only: refused while the gadget is shared (any admitted collaborator) and on the stopgap connection, at staging and again at apply before anything is sent, since InferOps records the sender as the approver. Self-approval is InferOps' to refuse, at apply, for good (CONFLICT). A proposal that cannot be shown in full on the approval card is refused at staging. Retry, for this operation (unlike the shared FORBIDDEN entry below): a FORBIDDEN proven not to have taken effect, whether refused before sending (a shared gadget, the stopgap) or refused by InferOps with its envelope (no knowledge:publish), leaves the action pending and retryable, and a later apply sends it once unshared or granted. A first attempt refused as stale, self-approval, already decided or needing a parent ends it failed, not retryable. Once an attempt may have reached InferOps (no answer, or a lost response), the outcome is unknown: it is resent under the same key while InferOps' answer could still help (InferOps replays the same principal and hash), even when a later check refuses it before sending, and a refusal that will stand ends it unknown and not retryable, never not-applied.

resources.scope: One custom table, by id, in one InferOps workspace the signed-in person holds; per-person sign-in only (no stopgap connection), or the mock's demo table. Every row read goes through InferOps' object.embed with a reference built from the binding's props, so InferOps checks the exact <tenant>.<workspace> against the reader on each read; the governed describe and list read the definition alone through table.get, in the workspace the client was opened for from that host. Read-only: no writes. Personal columns are projected out of every read, without a trace.

reads.notes: The definition without personal columns.
Up to 50 rows, newest first, with the definition from the same read; relatedTo narrows to rows linked to one endpoint. No filter on column values.
One row of the bound table, with the definition from the same read; a row of another table is NOT_FOUND.
FAC-9 governed read: the visible columns as fields, from the definition alone (table.get, no rows).

FAC-9 governed read: a request is checked against the definition alone before any row is read, then rows are read once and checked again against their own definition; filtered, sorted and paged in the gatekeeper over the newest 50.
FAC-9 governed read: getRecord's read; a row of another table, or none, is null.

resources.scope: The member list of one InferOps workspace the signed-in person holds (InferOps workspaces only); per-person sign-in only (no stopgap connection), or the mock's demo list. Every read is InferOps' member.list (GET /workspace/members) with the person's own token in the bound workspace, so InferOps' member:read, explicit denies and RLS decide. Read-only: no writes. Email is projected out of every read; names and ids remain.

reads.notes: The bound workspace's grant holders in InferOps' order: principal id, kind, name, role and explicit denies there; no email.

resources.scope: The published content-workflow policy of one project, by key, in one InferOps workspace the signed-in person holds; per-person sign-in only (no stopgap connection), or the mock's demo policy. An InferOS-minted binding URL that never reaches InferOps. Every read is exactly two GETs with the person's own token in the bound workspace: InferOps' project.list (GET /project/projects) to resolve the key there, then workflow.get (GET /project/projects/:projectId/workflow?workflow=content) for that project, so InferOps' project:read, explicit denies and RLS decide. Read-only: no writes. Every rule reason, the policy's agents and the head's publishedBy are projected out; principal ids in subjects remain.

reads.notes: The project's policy head as InferOps answered it, parsed strictly and fresh on every call, without rule reasons, agents or publishedBy; compiledHash is InferOps' hash of its compiled source policy, not of this projection.

resources.scope: The signed-in person's own Dot in one InferOps workspace they hold; per-person sign-in only (no stopgap connection, no demo). InferOps runs the Dot as the person (its chatbot domain and shared-agentic), re-authorizing every tool call and only ever proposing a write; a page or record the person names is read there as them, and one they can't open refuses the turn. InferOS keeps conversation ids and its decision on each proposal, never messages.

reads.notes: One turn through InferOps' streaming run route (POST /chatbot/conversations/:id/runs, AG-UI 1.0.2 over SSE), relayed event by event once @ag-ui/core's schema accepts it, under a 130 s deadline, a 35 s silence limit and size caps; a malformed or oversized event, a cut stream and the deadline each end the turn visibly. Logged as one observation, "Asked your Dot: <prompt>".
chatbot.conversation_get: the conversation's newest messages and its proposals, with InferOps' derived expired and unknown statuses.
chatbot.conversation_create; returns a session, no data.
chatbot.conversation_get, to prove it is the person's own; returns a session, no data.
chatbot.conversation_cancel on the running turn; what was said is kept, marked interrupted.

writes.notes: Each proposal a turn (or a later read) shows is staged once and submitted as an ordinary write, never auto-approvable. Approving it calls chatbot.proposal_confirm under the person's own token, keyed by the proposal id, which InferOps applies at most once; a confirm InferOps answers as already decided is read back and settled to its real status. Rejecting it calls chatbot.proposal_decline. Not revertible here.

resources.scope: Every InferOps board and InferMind Wiki the signed-in person's own account can open in one organization (inferos ADR 0015). The props hold the account and the tenant label only. Each openBoard/openWiki parses the reference with its own kind's grammar (so dispatch, workflow, table, members and page references are refused), requires the binding's tenant label, resolves the workspace slug among the person's own workspaces of the right product, and confirms the project or Wiki with their own token; every refusal is one NOT_FOUND. The sessions it opens are the board and Wiki sessions, fixed to what was opened. The demo account (inferops://demo.local/account) serves the mock; the stopgap connection is refused. Coding dispatch, workflow policy, custom tables and members keep their own bindings, and Operate keeps exact board bindings.

reads.notes: The person's workspaces in the organization. Withheld: every current collaborator is excluded, and once it is recorded the binding is owner-only for good (no collaborator is admitted after it).

As the board session's search, across the person's InferOps workspaces in the organization. Withheld as listWorkspaces is: the binding is owner-only from then on. So are findBoards on a board it opened and readDocumentText on a Wiki it opened.
Not an observation: narrows to one board. Its session's reads are observations of that board's data set (strategy C).
Not an observation: narrows to one Wiki. Its session's reads are observations of that Wiki's data set (strategy C).

approval.rejection: Deletes the pending record, which ends its simulation; a later apply of that id is refused as unknown.
approval.notes: Every write is checked against the simulated state, recorded with the exact request it will send and that request's fingerprint, and submitted as an action. Apply recomputes the fingerprint and refuses a mismatch before anything is sent, then sends under <facet instance id>:<action id> as the idempotency key. Applying an applied action is a no-op. An account binding's actions are proposed through the board and Wiki sessions it opens: each record carries its resolved target (kind, host, workspace id, project key), the fingerprint covers it, records are kept per target and indexed by the binding-wide action id, and apply and revert resolve the workspace again and refuse one that changed.

providerErrors.meaning: The project, issue, run, page or section does not exist or is outside the binding's scope; the two are indistinguishable.
The target changed after the write was proposed (an expected revision, section version or page version no longer matches; InferOps' page STALE_VERSION).
The target state belongs to the other workflow.
The target state is not part of the bound project.
A key was reused for a different change, or the stored request no longer matches its fingerprint.
The request itself was malformed (for instance a non-decimal revision or an empty title).
Refused in the target's current condition, such as a second pending change of one issue, a Wiki proposal already decided, or an approval by the proposal's own requester or reviser.
The issue already has a queued or running coding run, or a dispatch waiting for approval.
The person's session ended, was revoked, or the account was disconnected.
The person lacks the InferOps permission, or the workspace lacks the product; or a Wiki proposal approval from a shared gadget or the stopgap connection, which stays pending until it is unshared.
InferOps could not be reached, answered unusably, or the connection changed mid-request. The action stays pending, and a retry sends the same idempotency key.
The deployment has the integration (or coding dispatch) turned off; the action stays pending until it is turned back on.

simulation.summary: Pending actions are stored beside the binding and overlaid on every read until applied or rejected: a move shows the issue in its target state, an update its new title and priority, a create a provisional card, a dispatch a pending run, a cancel a run marked pending, a section edit its new body, a page body edit its new body (marked pendingBody), a proposal approval its proposal (marked pending approve, in InferOps' own state).
limits: A pending change keeps the revision InferOps reported: InferOps revisions are positions in a shared ledger, so the revision a change will produce cannot be computed. An issue therefore carries at most one live pending change, and a second is refused with CONFLICT.
A pending create is a provisional card (id pending-<action id>, identifier <KEY>-new, revision "0") that openIssue does not accept.
An issue's description is never read, so a pending description change is not shown and cannot be reverted.
A section edit is applied as a read then a write; an edit made in InferMind between the two is overwritten (see the design's Open Questions).

credentials.name: INFERLAB_AUTH_ORIGIN
credentials.purpose: InferLab central-auth origin. Set, every account is a person's own InferLab session (PKCE sign-in, held in InferOpsCredentials); unset, accounts are auto-provisioned demo accounts.

credentials.name: BASE_URL
credentials.purpose: This gatekeeper's public URL, for the sign-in redirect.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_BASE_URL
credentials.purpose: The InferOps API a connected person calls with their own token.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_API_TOKEN
credentials.purpose: Local-development stopgap connection shared by accounts with no identity. Never backs a connected person.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_WORKSPACE_SLUG
credentials.purpose: The workspace slug a URL must name to use the stopgap connection.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_COMPANY
credentials.purpose: The one company this deployment belongs to: an InferOps tenant id, or internal (reserved tenants only). InferOps refuses a session in any other company at the token exchange (auth.sso.inferosCompanies); with a tenant id the gatekeeper also refuses a sign-in, connect, reconnect or stored connection in another one. Grants nothing.
credentials.default: Unset: InferOps alone decides (local development). Set but malformed: sign-in is off.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_ENABLED
credentials.purpose: Capability switch for the whole integration, checked on every call.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_TABLES_ENABLED
credentials.purpose: Capability switch for object/table, checked on every call.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_MEMBERS_ENABLED
credentials.purpose: Capability switch for portal/members, checked on every call.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_DOT_ENABLED
credentials.purpose: Capability switch for chatbot/dot, checked on every call.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_WORKFLOW_POLICY_ENABLED
credentials.purpose: Capability switch for project/workflow, checked on every call.

credentials.name: INFEROPS_HOST_BOARDS
credentials.purpose: Proposed switch for the board facet's kernel-only host-board read (project.board_snapshot), checked on every call. Adds no resource kind.

credentials.name: CODING_WORKBENCH_REPOS
credentials.purpose: Comma-separated InferOps repository ids a dispatch may target.

provider.name: InferOps
provider.notes: The InferOps HTTP API is unversioned; compatibility is pinned by the generated board DTO schema below. Endpoints this client calls beyond the board (issues, runs, repos, knowledge) are not yet covered by a generated contract. The Wiki structure read, page body/version/masterRole and the strict page-body write need InferOps at or after c536b63718478842a1b163b473eb03b16dd7f9b7 (factory-level/inferops#2345); the revision above stays the board-schema pin. Wiki proposal reads and approval need InferOps at or after 5483e7cd (factory-level/inferops#2368) with knowledge.wikiPublish.enabled on; otherwise those calls are NOT_FOUND. Wiki search (searchWiki) needs InferOps at or after a2f27606 (factory-level/inferops#2563, knowledge.search); against an earlier one every search is UNAVAILABLE, never an empty list. The console widget index (`PUT` and `DELETE /knowledge/widget-definitions`, `widget.publish` and `widget.withdraw`) needs InferOps at or after 1d68de3591900c44212db8a05239241f9819b1b1 (factory-level/inferops#2573). Admitting a workflow run on request (`holdsWorkflowInvoke`, `workflow:invoke`) needs InferOps at or after b850dd5afa33ae88ef1422c69e6c801c28d70b89 (factory-level/inferops#2586); against an earlier one nobody holds it, so every run on request is refused where SHARED_CONFIGURATION_GATEKEEPER names InferOps. Named service queries (`GET /object/queries/:name?queryVersion=1`) and the service dashboard's governed comment (`POST /project/issues/:issueId/comments` with `expectedIssueHeadSeq`) require InferOps at or after c3261767bf0dfeaf555fe0e364da74b1c91a20c9 (factory-level/inferops#2596), with objects enabled and an explicitly configured nonproduction company data plane. The query names are service-jobs, service-job-status-counts and service-job-recent-activities. Earlier or unsupported providers return unavailable; widgets do not treat that as an empty result. Widget search by intent (`searchWidgets`, `GET /knowledge/widget-search`, `widget.search`) needs InferOps at or after 4e913afefffcabd5175442050c9dc0f7d3c75e86 (factory-level/inferops#2617); against an earlier one it is UNAVAILABLE, never an empty result. The revision above remains the generated board-schema pin. The Dot (chatbot/dot) needs InferOps at or after 0c09fa9b648150257e745e22c2032bc5d57d46fc (factory-level/inferops#2618, which carries #2619), with the FAC-133 conversation and proposal capabilities (chatbot.conversation_create, _get, _run and _cancel, chatbot.proposal_list, _confirm and _decline, the server-checked selection, the keyed confirm and the derived expired and unknown statuses). Its company-wide knowledge reads and its page edit and create proposals (FAC-136) need InferOps at or after 97e335ea6f47b890a18143eb813b4b2b158194ad (factory-level/inferops#2622), which the revision above includes. Dot run outcomes (Gatekeeper.workflowRunOutcome to chatbot.proposal_run_outcome, factory-level/inferops#2644) and the run named at a hand-off confirmation ({runId}) require InferOps at or after df4794f91200a8d1a3cb9fe2b88de4e658c1087d; against an earlier revision the outcome call returns NOT_FOUND (the provider retries, then marks it undelivered), and a confirmation runId is rejected or ignored.

perConnector.reason: The shared suite revokes a demo account over MockInferOps. A connected person's revocation (InferLab sign-out, UNAUTHORIZED on the next read) goes through the HTTP client and InferLab, which the suite's adapter does not fake.

No shared-suite adapter yet: dispatch needs the coding-workbench switch and repository allowlist set per test. Its own suite covers these cases; account.test.ts also verifies that a stored connection from another deployment company is refused before dispatch project lookup.

No shared-suite adapter yet. Its section write is guarded by a read before the write, so a retry after a lost response is answered by that re-read; its page body write by InferOps' compare-and-swap and same-key replay; its proposal approval by InferOps' principal-and-hash replay. Its own suite covers these cases.
Not tested for this kind. It reads through the same data source and account credentials as project/board, whose revocation and UNAVAILABLE handling the shared suite covers.
Not tested for this kind. It reads through the same data source and account credentials as project/board, whose revocation and UNAVAILABLE handling the shared suite covers.
Read-only and private-only: the shared suite's adapter assumes writes and an admissible collaborator, so this kind has its own suite. Sharing is the private-only refusal (addObserver always throws).
Not applicable: the kind proposes no writes, so there is nothing to approve, apply or retry. Its tests assert the mock and the HTTP client see no non-GET request.

Read-only and private-only: its session lists one bound workspace, observations exclude member identity, sharing is refused, and account revocation stops reads. account.test.ts also verifies that a stored connection from another deployment company is refused before the members probe. There are no writes, revisions, or write retries to express in the shared suite.
Not applicable: this read-only resource has no write path. Provider read failures return unavailable and are not retried as writes.

Read-only and private-only: its session reads the bound project's policy projection, observes each read, refuses sharing, and stops after account revocation. There are no writes, revisions, or write retries to express in the shared suite.
Not applicable: this read-only resource has no write path. Provider read failures return unavailable and are not retried as writes.

No shared-suite adapter yet: the shared cases assume a session that writes directly, and this kind's writes go through the board and Wiki sessions it opens. Its own suites cover opening and every refusal, per-target pending actions, routing of apply, reject and revert, the fingerprinted target, the workspace check at apply, and strategy C admission and exclusion.

Not tested for this kind. Apply, revert and retry run the same board and Wiki functions over the same data source and account credentials as project/board and knowledge/wiki, whose cases are covered there.
